messages:
maria: Kicking off eu-west6 bring-up now. Follow runbook: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/eu-west6-bootstrap. Please monitor node bootstrap and GPU driver jobs. tagging @infra-oncall

jamal: saw terraform apply fail in the middle of subnet creation earlier. pushing a retry now. error was ENI quota exceeded in region.

deploy-bot: terraform apply failed: 
```
Error: creating NetworkInterface: InvalidParameterValue: Failed to allocate address for ENI: quota exceeded
```

alex: I can repro node kubelet crashloops on one of the new instances — kubelet logs show cgroup driver mismatch vs containerd. quick grep: `cgroupfs vs systemd`

emma: also seeing GPU plugin DaemonSet crashbackoff on new g4dn nodes. gpu-driver-install init container exits with code 1. logs: "nvidia: no compatible devices found"

maria: ok two parallel issues: (1) ENI/quota causing partial subnet failures; (2) host-level driver mismatch / GPU driver not binding. rolling back the latest ami change? Jamal, keep retrying quota request with cloud team.

jamal: filed ticket with cloud-quotas@cloud (ref CQ-4821). ETA 45m for quota bump in eu-west6. meanwhile I'm marking failing subnets with tag `bringup:blocked` so the operator won't keep retrying.

alex: quick debug: nodes boot OK when using previous AMI (ami-0abc1234). New AMI has `containerd` built with cgroupfs default. we can patch kubelet config or rebuild image. Suggest reverting AMI in autoscaling launch config to ami-0abc1234 to get pods schedulable.

emma: for GPU plugin: I dumped `lspci` output on one instance — PCI device visible but driver install script expects kernel >=5.10. The build image shipped kernel 5.4. That's why nvidia modules fail.

maria: that's a clear mismatch. Two remediation paths: (A) revert to previous AMI (fast) to unblock workloads; (B) rebuild AMI with newer kernel + containerd systemd cgroup config (longer). I vote revert and then schedule image rebuild.

infra-oncall: rolling revert on ASG/Launch Configuration now for the gpu-pool-autoscaling group. will cordon and drain any nodes that show problems after new nodes join.

deploy-bot: ASG update triggered: `update-auto-scaling-group gpu-pool-autoscaling -> launch_template ami-0abc1234` (operation id op-99231)

jamal: ENI quota still blocking the remaining subnet allocations — quota bump pending. If quota not in by 45m we should split pool across existing subnets (workaround) or delay bring-up. Cost note: splitting across AZs will increase cross-AZ data egress slightly.

alex: after revert started, I see kubelet stabilized on 3 nodes. GPU plugin reports devices present, and the nvidia driver pod moves to Running on two nodes. still one stuck with kernel mismatch (probably the bad AMI slipped in one bucket).

emma: manual node remediation: for the stuck instance I ssh'd in and confirmed kernel 5.4. we should fail that host out of rolling group. tag `bad-ami:yes` and terminate.

maria: agreed. Jamal, mark the host and terminate once cordon/evict complete. Also update the runbook note about AMI version pinning under "image-validation" step — add a check for kernel version + containerd cgroup config.

jamal: done: host i-0f4b2c marked, terminating now. updated runbook entry: "validate: uname -r >= 5.10 && containerd cgroup = systemd".

infra-oncall: quota bump confirmed (CQ-4821 resolved). Subnet creation retried and completed.

maria: final status: ENI quota resolved, AMI revert unblocks fleet, one bad instance terminated. still need formal image rebuild and a patch to image validation in CI. action items: (1) infra: create AMI-rebuild ticket with kernel/containerd fix; (2) devex: add AMI validation step in new-region runbook; (3) ops: run a second bring-up tomorrow for capacity soak.

alex: adding steps to admissions test: `kubectl get nodes -o wide` + `kubectl get daemonset nvidia-driver -n kube-system -o jsonpath='{.status.numberReady}'`

emma: will follow-up on driver install logs and open a driver hook issue so future images run module compile on boot.

maria: thanks everyone. closing this thread — will reopen if anything flares during soak. :white_check_mark:
